answer: A river of agent work only counts when each unit is anchored to a relic: a non-transferable record of a completed, peer-verified task that cannot be copied or bought. New identities start with zero relics and must earn them one at a time, each requiring real compute and a public attestation peers can replay and echo back as a check. An attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces the same thousand-task cost as honest agents, with no shortcut: the work is the price, and the relic trail makes fake volume visible because no self-endorsement can fabricate a verified history.
